active.description: On Temurin 17 with pyspark 3.5.8 the three Arrow tests pass without the extraJavaOptions netty reflection flag and java.nio --add-opens, because Spark's launcher adds the opens itself (the 0.8.1 PLAN M4 failure was Java 21). active.title: Text generation performance follow-ups after the Arrow rewrite
active.description: (1) dates with time directives is only ~1.2x faster than 0.8.0 (7.71 s -> 6.28 s at 10M rows, measured in J3.T6) against ~25x for date-only, because each time field runs per-row digit loops; candidate: a two-digit pair table per field, as int_zfilled already does; 0.8.1 AC1.3 covered date-only only. (2) uuid4 in rand_engine/core/_np_core.py hex-encodes through bytes.hex().encode(), ~640 MB of temporaries at 10M rows; binascii.hexlify writes the hex bytes directly. (3) zero-row uuid4 and int_zfilled now return an empty Arrow column (0.8.0: empty float64, and a raise) and no test pins it; add the zero-size partition to their contract tests. 2026-10-31: (1) is re-judged after native-datetime-output (0.9.0 rc-3), since a native date/time column needs no per-field digit loop; a change to gen_dates needs its by-name approval (invariant 12).

active.title: One shared virtualenv for the repo's verify gate
active.description: The verify: line in the repo AGENTS.md sets POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_IN_PROJECT=false with one shared poetry cache, so poetry builds a ~0.66 GB virtualenv per worktree path and nothing removes it when the tree is dropped; on 2026-10-20 70 orphaned environments (43 GB) filled the disk. Design: one shared environment that every tree's verify: reuses (for example POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_CREATE=false inside one environment kept under the shared cache), not one per path. This changes the verify: gate, so the operator rules on it with its measured cost per run against the current line (a cold and a warm run of each).

active.title: Mandatory hardware study: chunk size vs speed and peak memory, presented before any implementation
active.description: Horizon: 0.9.0 rc-4, first, before 1.0 (operator 2026-10-31: "Memória: estudo + teto 1 GB (Recomendado)"; order: release-1-0). Operator answer (verbatim): "devemos fazer em pedaços, mas devemos observar e fazer um estudo serio sobre o trade-off de velocidade vs montar em pedaçõ e fazer append, se usamos o disco, como usamos, quais seriam os chunks otimizados para que mantenhamos a velocidade e reduzimos. ... é obrigatorio vc me apresentar esse estudo ... um grafico onde temos eixos com o tamanho do chunk e a velocidade ... pelo menos 3 estrategias ... Oferecer como default memoria máxima consumida de 1GB. E usuário consegue passar alterar, diminuir, isso afetará no tamanho de chunks, devemos ter as estimativas de velocidade de geração para aquele tamanho de chunk." Outcome: a study presented to the operator before any chunked-output implementation, naming the winning strategy and chunk size per memory budget: a chunk-size sweep 10^3..10^8 rows, x = chunk size, y = throughput (rows/µs, MB/s), a second panel with peak RSS; at least 3 strategies among monolithic, sequential chunks + append, multiprocessing parts, threads with per-block Generators, and Python 3.14 free-threaded if the ecosystem supports it; interfering variables isolated (cache sizes, column types, format/codec, row-group size, workers, per-chunk fixed cost, page cache, disk type); hardware measured (CPU, caches, RAM bandwidth, disk write); per-block Philox streams tested so seeds are independent of chunk size and thread count. Out of scope: changing the library's generation or writers; the study is the operator's decision input. Seed (2026-10-31): the study measures against seed-per-column (0.9.0 rc-1); a seed guarantee across threads or processes is not a 1.0 contract (a counter-based per-row seed is the 2.0 path).

active.title: Output speed first under a bounded memory budget
active.description: Horizon: 0.9.0 rc-4, after hardware-chunk-study, before 1.0 since it changes a default (operator 2026-10-31: "Memória: estudo + teto 1 GB (Recomendado)"). E usuário consegue passar alterar, diminuir, isso afetará no tamanho de chunks, devemos ter as estimativas de velocidade de geração para aquele tamanho de chunk." Outcome: output built from the study's winning strategy: a memory budget, default 1 GB and user-adjustable, sets the chunk size from the measured bytes/row table; writers and stream obey it; get_df refuses an estimated frame above it with the estimate in the message; max_memory=None disables it; parallel part writing, Arrow-direct Parquet/CSV, vectorized JSON; gen.plan(max_memory=...) returns chunk rows, expected peak and throughput without measuring; `rand-engine benchmark --max-memory 1GB` measures the user's machine (~1 min); the docs publish the study curves on reference hardware. Any draw-order change beyond seed-per-column (0.9.0 rc-1) is a seed-contract revision in its SPEC (invariant 4). Measured motivation (CI): columns 7-512 rows/µs vs CSV 3, Parquet 2.4, JSON 0.5, stream_dict 0.17 rows/µs. Out of scope: the stream rate contract (stream-rate-per-microbatch), text-method speed (text-perf-follow-ups), a native core, a new runtime dependency.

active.title: Seed contract: one random generator per column, from the seed and the column name
active.description: Horizon: 0.9.0 rc-1 (contract core). Operator answer (verbatim): "Um gerador por coluna (Recomendado)". Outcome: each column draws from its own generator derived from the seed and the column name, so adding a column leaves the other columns unchanged and batch generation (stream, maxRowsPerBatch) gives the get_df values for the chunk-invariant methods; every seeded value changes once in 0.9.0; the gen_* functions stay untouched. Measured at feature/0.8.1 3fcd389: adding a column in front changes every other column, and 1x1000 vs 10x100 rows differ for 14 of 15 ordinary methods (only constant equal); a prototype with one SeedSequence([seed, crc32(name)]) stream per column made 13 of 15 chunk-invariant, poisson and zipf still differing through _alias_draw's two draws per call (not operator code). The 0.9.0 SPEC revises invariant 4; ADR 0004 (seed contract) is proposed with its rc, its measured_by the chunk/column-independence contract test that rc writes, and the operator accepts it at that rc's closure. Out of scope: a seed guarantee across parallel processes or Spark partitions (a counter-based per-row seed is the 2.0 path).
